- What the FOMC said: The Committee held the target range at 5.25–5.50%, kept IOER at 5.4%, and continued QT. It acknowledged “further progress” toward 2% inflation and a “better balance” of risks but kept cuts contingent on “greater confidence” that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%.
- What the Beige Book adds: The latest Beige Book (compiled by the Richmond Fed with information through early July) indicates overall activity was modest and uneven across Districts. Contacts reported:
  - Labor markets continuing to loosen and wage pressures easing compared with earlier in the year.
  - Price increases moderating to a more modest pace.
  - Softer momentum in several service sectors and continued manufacturing softness in some Districts.
  - Persistent CRE stress—especially offices—and tight credit conditions; bank lending standards remained restrictive with tepid loan demand.
- Interpretation: Beige Book evidence of moderating wages/prices and softening in services/manufacturing reinforces that policy is restrictive and working. Coupled with tight credit and CRE headwinds, this reduces the need for additional tightening but doesn’t yet deliver the “greater confidence” needed for cuts. Net tone remains cautiously constructive on disinflation but tempered by growth and stability risks.

Adjusted tone: mildly positive-to-neutral, slightly more cautious than before given broad-based softness and tight credit.
